prompt: Why is the outbox row written in the same transaction as the session it describes?

choices.text: The server reads the device's transaction log during sync
choices.why: The server never sees the device's database.

choices.text: Transactions make the two inserts faster than separate ones
choices.why: They can, but that is not why it matters here.

choices.text: So a crash between them cannot strand a change
choices.why: Right. The two land together or neither does.

choices.text: SQLite refuses two separate writes
choices.why: It accepts them; the risk is the moment between them.

prompt: What does each outbox row's `body` hold in the lesson's planner?

choices.text: The whole row as it stood after the change
choices.why: Right, and a delete has no body.

choices.text: The HTTP request exactly as it will be sent, headers included
choices.why: The outbox holds changes to the data, not requests.

choices.text: The difference from the previous version, such as +5 minutes
choices.why: That would make coalescing unsafe; the lesson sends the whole row.

choices.text: Nothing; the drain reads the session table
choices.why: Then a deleted session could not be described, and an older version would be lost.

prompt: Why does the lesson's outbox use AUTOINCREMENT on `seq` rather than a plain integer primary key?

choices.text: Without it, SQLite would store the rows in random order
choices.why: The query orders by seq; storage order is not the issue.

choices.text: The server needs the numbers to be global
choices.why: seq never leaves the device.

choices.text: It is the only way to have a primary key in SQLite
choices.why: Any column can be a primary key.

choices.text: A deleted number is never reused, so a later operation never sorts first
choices.why: Right. Without it, SQLite may reuse the highest number after a delete.

prompt: With no server running, what did `drain.ts` do with operations #2 and #3?

choices.text: Sent them in parallel and reported both as failed
choices.why: It sends one at a time.

choices.text: Nothing: it stopped at #1
choices.why: Right. Both depend on #1 having arrived.

choices.text: Deleted them, since the session is already on the device
choices.why: That would lose the changes the server needs.

choices.text: Moved them to the dead table
choices.why: Dead is for 4xx answers, not for a missing network.

prompt: Why not send the whole outbox in parallel to save time?

choices.text: The server accepts one connection at a time
choices.why: Node's server takes many; the risk is the order.

choices.text: Nothing guarantees two operations on one session arrive in order
choices.why: Right. An update before its create is a 404.

choices.text: Parallel requests use more data
choices.why: The same bytes are sent either way.

choices.text: fetch in Node has no way to start several requests at the same moment
choices.why: It can; Promise.all would do it.

prompt: Put the requests in the order the server's terminal printed them after the drain.
Which answers make `drain.ts` stop and leave the operation for the next run? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the network failing before any answer
choices.why: That is the train.

choices.text: a 503 from the server
choices.why: A 5xx stops the drain too.

choices.text: a 422 from the server
choices.why: A 4xx moves the operation to dead and the drain carries on.

choices.text: a 201 from the server
choices.why: Success removes the row and moves on.

prompt: A session is created and then deleted before any drain runs. What does compaction leave for it?

choices.text: A delete, so the server removes it
choices.why: The server never had it; a delete would be a 404.

choices.text: Both, in order, since a delete is an event that must arrive
choices.why: A delete of a row the server never saw tells it nothing.

choices.text: A create, so the server keeps a record of it
choices.why: The person deleted it; the server should not receive it.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. Both operations go.

prompt: In the lesson's run, how many operations did `compact.ts` leave in the outbox?
A team's outbox carries operations such as 'add 25 minutes to this week's total'. What does the lesson say about coalescing them?

choices.text: Do not fold them: each is an event and has to arrive
choices.why: Right. Two of them could only become one by adding them, which is a different rule.

choices.text: Keep the first one, since it was queued earliest
choices.why: Same loss, the other way round.

choices.text: Keep the last one, as for the planner's updates
choices.why: That drops minutes: each one is a step, not a new version.

choices.text: Fold them if they are less than a minute apart
choices.why: Time apart changes nothing about what they say.

prompt: A compaction rule is right only if the server ends in the same ___ as it would by receiving every operation.
What does the lesson call an operation the server will refuse every time it is sent?

choices.text: A tombstone
choices.why: A tombstone records a delete, in lesson 11.

choices.text: A conflict
choices.why: A conflict is two changes to one row, in lesson 13.

choices.text: Poison
choices.why: Right. It blocks everything behind it until it is moved aside.

choices.text: A backoff
choices.why: Backoff is how long to wait between tries, in lesson 9.

prompt: In the run, `#10 update s11` was valid and still not sent. Why?

choices.text: The create it updates was dead, so the server has no s11
choices.why: Right. Sent, it would have been a 404.

choices.text: The server was down by then
choices.why: #11 was sent after it and got 201.

choices.text: 200 minutes is over the server's limit
choices.why: The limit is 240.

choices.text: Updates wait until every create in the outbox has been sent and accepted
choices.why: Only updates to the same session wait.

prompt: Match what the server answered to what `drain.ts` does with the operation.

pairs.right: moves it to dead and carries on
leaves it and stops, as for a 5xx

prompt: Why does a 422 go to `dead` instead of being retried on the next drain?

choices.text: To save battery on the next drain
choices.why: Battery is a side effect; the reason is the answer itself.

choices.text: The server forgets the operation after a 422, so a retry would be meaningless
choices.why: The server's memory is not the issue; the same bytes get the same answer.

choices.text: The server read it and said no, and will say no to the same bytes again
choices.why: Right. Retrying is a loop that holds everything behind it.

choices.text: Because 4xx means the network failed
choices.why: A 4xx is an answer, so the network worked.

prompt: A planner's outbox holds `#1 create s20`, `#2 update s20`, `#3 delete s20`, `#4 create s21`. Compaction runs. What reaches the server when it drains?

choices.text: A delete of s20 and a create of s21
choices.why: s20 was created in the same queue; the server never had it.

choices.text: Only a create of s21
choices.why: Right. #2 folds into #1, and the create and delete then cancel out.

choices.text: A create of s20 with the updated body, then s21
choices.why: The delete came after; the session no longer exists.

choices.text: All four, since compaction leaves deletes alone
choices.why: It handles deletes, two different ways.

prompt: A release ships a bug that sends `minutes` as a string, and every create now gets a 400. What does the lesson's design make visible, and where?

choices.text: Nothing: the drain stops at the first 400 and waits for the network
choices.why: A 4xx does not stop the drain; it moves the operation to dead.

choices.text: A crash on every phone at once, since a 400 throws
choices.why: fetch resolves with the 400; drain.ts reads its status.

choices.text: Sessions retried every minute until the bug is fixed
choices.why: Dead operations are not retried by the drain.

choices.text: A count of dead operations rising on every phone, each with the server's reason
choices.why: Right. That count, reported by the app, is how the team finds out the same day.

prompt: A drain and a compaction start at the same moment on one phone. Which could go wrong? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: an update folded into a create the drain has already sent
choices.why: The server then never receives the update.

choices.text: the server receiving an update for a session it never got
choices.why: The lesson's example of the race.

choices.text: SQLite refusing both programs because two are open
choices.why: SQLite allows several connections; the trouble is the logic.

choices.text: the dead table filling with valid operations
choices.why: Dead is filled by 4xx answers, which a race does not cause.
